6171-memorials-and-other-papers-complete.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Many of the papers in my collected works were originally written under one set of disadvantages, and are now revised under another. They were written generally under great pressure as to time, in order to catch the critical periods of monthly journals; written oftentimes at a distance from the press (so as to have no opportunity for correction); and always written at a distance from libraries, so that very many statements, references, and citations, were made on the authority of my unassisted memory.

arxiv-2105-12553.title: Highlights of Discoveries for δ \delta Scuti Variable Stars from the Kepler Era
arxiv-2105-12553.creator: Joyce Ann Guzik 1,∗
arxiv-2105-12553.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Joyce Ann Guzik 1,∗. The NASA Kepler and follow-on K2 mission (2009-2018) left a legacy of data and discoveries, finding thousands of exoplanets, and also obtaining high-precision long time-series data for hundreds of thousands of stars, including many types of pulsating variables. Here we highlight a few of the ongoing discoveries from Kepler data on δ \delta Scuti pulsating variables, which are core hydrogen-burning stars of about twice the mass of the Sun.

arxiv-2201-08799.title: GHz-Pulsed Source of Entangled Photons for Reconfigurable Quantum Networks
arxiv-2201-08799.creator: Meritxell Cabrejo Ponce, Christopher Spiess, André Luiz Marques Muniz and Philippe Ancsin, Fabian Steinlechner
arxiv-2201-08799.description: Abstract Entanglement is a universal resource in quantum networks, yet entangled photon sources are typically custom-made for a specific use case. Versatility, both in terms of state modulation and tunability of the temporal properties of the photons, is the key to flexible network architectures and cryptographic primitives that go beyond quantum key distribution.

arxiv-2206-15088.title: On graphs coverable by k k shortest paths
arxiv-2206-15088.creator: Maël Dumas, Florent Foucaud, Anthony Perez, Ioan Todinca
arxiv-2206-15088.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Maël Dumas, Florent Foucaud, Anthony Perez, Ioan Todinca. We show that if the edges or vertices of an undirected graph G G can be covered by k k shortest paths, then the pathwidth of G G is upper-bounded by a single-exponential function of k k .

arxiv-2207-12686.title: Exponential asymptotic stability of Riemann shocks of hyperbolic systems of balance laws Thanks: G.F. acknowledges support from the ANR via the project Indyana under grant agreement ANR- 21- CE40-0008, Labex CIMI under grant agreement ANR-11-LABX-0040, and an ANITI (Artificial and Natural Intelligen
arxiv-2207-12686.creator: Grégory Faye, L. Miguel Rodrigues
arxiv-2207-12686.description: Abstract . For strictly entropic Riemann shock solutions of strictly hyperbolic systems of balance laws, we prove that exponential spectral stability implies large-time asymptotic orbital stability. As a preparation, we also prove similar results for constant solutions of initial value and initial boundary value problems, that seem to be new in this generality.

arxiv-2212-04661.title: An Attention-based Multi-Scale Feature Learning Network for Multimodal Medical Image Fusion
arxiv-2212-04661.creator: Meng Zhou, Xiaolan Xu, and Yuxuan Zhang
arxiv-2212-04661.description: Abstract Medical images play an important role in clinical applications. Multimodal medical images could provide rich information about patients for physicians to diagnose. The image fusion technique is able to synthesize complementary information from multimodal images into a single image.

arxiv-2312-07575.title: TapTree: Process-Tree based Host Behavior Modeling and Threat Detection Framework via Sequential Pattern Mining
arxiv-2312-07575.creator: Mohammad Mamun, Scott Buffett
arxiv-2312-07575.description: Abstract Host behaviour modelling is widely deployed in today’s corporate environments to aid in the detection and analysis of cyber attacks. Audit logs containing system-level events are frequently used for behavior modeling as they can provide detailed insight into cyber-threat occurrences.

arxiv-2408-13482.title: MPruner: Optimizing Neural Network Size with CKA-Based Mutual Information Pruning
arxiv-2408-13482.creator: Seungbeom Hu, ChanJun Park, Andrew Ferraiuolo, Sang-Ki Ko, Jinwoo Kim, Haein Song, Jieung Kim
arxiv-2408-13482.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Seungbeom Hu, ChanJun Park, Andrew Ferraiuolo, Sang-Ki Ko, Jinwoo Kim, Haein Song, Jieung Kim. Determining the optimal size of a neural network is critical, as it directly impacts runtime performance and memory usage. Pruning is a well-established model compression technique that reduces the size of neural networks while mathematically guaranteeing accuracy preservation. However, many recent pruning methods overlook the global contributions of individual model components, making it difficult to ensure that a pruned model meets the desired dataset and performance requirements.

arxiv-2502-19843.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Forward and Inverse PDEs with Limited and Noisy Data: Application to Solar Corona Modeling
arxiv-2502-19843.creator: Hubert Baty
arxiv-2502-19843.description: Abstract I will demonstrate the effectiveness of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) in solving partial differential equations (PDEs) when training data are scarce or noisy. The training data can be located either at the boundaries or within the domain. Additionally, PINNs can be used as an inverse method to determine unknown coefficients in the equations.

arxiv-2505-24563.title: Molecular chiral response enhanced by crosstalking quasi-bound states in the continuum
arxiv-2505-24563.creator: Diana Shakirova, Adrià Canós Valero, Daniil Riabov, Hatice Altug, Andrey Bogdanov, Thomas Weiss
arxiv-2505-24563.description: Abstract Identifying the handedness of chiral molecules is of fundamental importance in chemistry, biology, pharmacy, and medicine. Nanophotonic structures allow us to control light at the nanoscale and offer powerful tools for chiral sensing, enabling the detection of small analyte volumes and low molecular concentrations by harnessing optical resonances.

arxiv-2507-10733.title: 3S-Attack: Spatial, Spectral and Semantic Invisible Backdoor Attack Against DNN Models
arxiv-2507-10733.creator: Jianyao Yin, Luca Arnaboldi, Honglong Chen, Pascal Berrang
arxiv-2507-10733.description: Abstract Backdoor attacks involve either poisoning the training data or directly modifying the model in order to implant a hidden behavior, that causes the model to misclassify inputs when a specific trigger is present. During inference, the model maintains high accuracy on benign samples but misclassifies poisoned samples into an attacker-specified target class.

pmc-10688228.title: Computational Expansion of High-Resolution-MSn Spectral Libraries
pmc-10688228.creator: Brandon
pmc-10688228.description: Commonly, in MS-based untargeted metabolomics, some metabolites cannot be confidently identified due to ambiguities in resolving isobars and structurally similar species. To address this, analytical techniques beyond traditional MS2 analysis, such as MSn fragmentation, can be applied to probe metabolites for additional structural information.

pmc-11588567.title: Methods in causal inference. Part 1: causal diagrams and confounding
pmc-11588567.creator: Joseph A Bulbulia
pmc-11588567.description: Keywords: Causal inference, culture, DAGs, evolution, tutorial Media summary: Causal directed acyclic graphs (causal DAGs) are powerful tools for clarifying assumptions required for causal inference. However, they can be easily misused. This tutorial provides guidance on safely integrating causal diagrams into analytic workflows, underscoring the importance of starting with clearly defined causal questions.

pmc-11728963.title: Fall prevention among older adults in KSA: Role of physical therapy
pmc-11728963.creator: Ghadah M Algudairi, Abeer M Alrashed
pmc-11728963.description: ObjectivesFalls and fall-related injuries among older adults are a growing public health concern. Although multiple factors and co-morbidities are associated with falls, balance and gait disorders are among the most common causes. Physical therapists have expertise in fall-risk assessment and management. The purpose of this study was to assess the fall prevention services provided by physical therapists to older adults.

pmc-13059300.title: Replication of the Association between Retinal Aging Clock Susceptibility Genes and Retinal Age Gap in an Asian Population: The Nagahama Study
pmc-13059300.creator: Yoshifumi Komatsu, Takuro Kamei, Kazuya Morino, Shin-ya Nakao, Masahiro Akada, Keina Sado, Yuta Doi, Tomotaro Tanaka, Masayuki Hata, Yasuharu Tabara, Fumihiko Matsuda, Akitaka Tsujikawa, Masahiro Miyake
pmc-13059300.description: PurposeTo replicate previously reported genetic associations for the retinal aging clock—quantified as the retinal age gap—in an East Asian population and to assess cross-ancestry consistency of effect directions and sizes.DesignGenetic association study with candidate-single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) replication embedded in a population-based cohort.

pmc-13219030.title: Explaining hidden mechanisms: a generative model for causal graphs with nonlinear latent factors
pmc-13219030.creator: Koji Maruhashi, Heewon Park, Rui Yamaguchi, Satoru Miyano
pmc-13219030.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Biomedical data analysis can now recover large families of condition-specific causal graphs, yet these results are often too complex for humans to interpret mechanistically. To address this challenge, we adopt a generative perspective, we address this challenge by formulating a structural-equation-based generative model in which each observed graph is generated from a small number of latent causal mechanisms under a bidirectional causal-consistency constraint linking latent and observed causal effects.

pmc-13260409.title: Cholesterol synthases suppress metastasis and stemness through PDIA4/ACLY or SYVN1/SCD1 axis in advanced colorectal cancer
pmc-13260409.creator: Wenjie Li, Moubin Lin, Yun Zhao, Yuqi Tang, Ying Chen, Luwei He
pmc-13260409.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aberrant cholesterol biosynthesis is a notable hallmark of cancers, supporting unlimited cell proliferation. Previously, we delineated that cholesterol synthases FDFT1 and SQLE promoted colorectal cancer (CRC) cell proliferation, while how these enzymes influence CRC metastasis and stemness remains unclear. This study demonstrates that suppress of FDFT1 or SQLE enhances CRC metastasis and stemness through impairing ER stress and degrading PDIA4 or SYVN1 individually. Additionally, the function of FDFT1 and SQLE on CRC metastasis relies on tryptophan.
